newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen firm at open as FOMC meets.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen firm at open as FOMC meets.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open steady to higher Wednesday, with investors nearly certain that Federal Reserve policymakers, wrapping up a two-day meeting, would not raise interest rates.
The Federal Open Market Committee is expected to announce its verdict at around 1815 GMT, but none of the 36 economists surveyed by Reuters expect the Fed to tighten credit.

"The consensus appears to be steady as she goes for the market," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co said. "Most players believe there is little likelihood the Fed will raise rates here."
U.S. blue chip stocks and bonds rose yesterday as weaker-than-forecast manufacturing data heightened expectations the Federal Reserve would leave rates alone.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished up 49.54 points at 7,722.33 on Tuesday.

"The only surprise here would be if the Fed raised rates," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments said. He said stock market valuations already assumed the Federal Reserve would not raise rates.
Stocks and bonds were also awaiting a key employment report for June, due out on Thursday, for any sign of wage inflation, analysts said.
